pointers.sentence: A server imports the project's `wsgi.py` or `asgi.py`, which makes the handler by calling one of the two functions; each runs `django.setup` first (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).

A server imports the project's `wsgi.py` or `asgi.py`, which makes the handler by calling one of the two functions; each runs `django.setup` first (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).
It then calls the server's function with the status line and the headers, and returns the response (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).
`BaseHandler.get_response` is a thin shell around the chain's call (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

After it, it adds the request's `close`, which closes its uploaded files, to the response's closers, the functions the response's `close` calls, and passes a response of 400 or above to `log_response` (`django/utils/log.py:log_response`).

By the docstring of `BaseHandler.get_response_async`, one asynchronous `get_response` for everything, WSGI included, is too slow, and a separate path avoids the context switch (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response_async`): under WSGI no event loop is running, and `async_to_sync` then runs a coroutine on a new loop in a new thread while the calling thread waits (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:AsyncToSync.__call__`).

By the docstring of `BaseHandler.get_response_async`, one asynchronous `get_response` for everything, WSGI included, is too slow, and a separate path avoids the context switch (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response_async`): under WSGI no event loop is running, and `async_to_sync` then runs a coroutine on a new loop in a new thread while the calling thread waits (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:AsyncToSync.__call__`).
`HttpResponseBase.close` runs every closer registered on the response, the request's among them, and then sends `request_finished` (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.close`).
*The three signals of the request cycle, defined in `django/core/signals.py`.*

`ASGIHandler.__call__` accepts only a scope of the type `"http"` and runs `ASGIHandler.handle` inside asgiref's `ThreadSensitiveContext`, which gives the request's synchronous code a thread of its own ([Sync and async in one chain](async.md#one-thread-per-request)) (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.__call__`).

At a disconnect the listener raises `RequestAborted` (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.listen_for_disconnect`), and the group cancels `handle`'s own task where it waits; leaving its block, it withdraws that cancellation and raises the `RequestAborted` in an exception group (`asyncio.TaskGroup`).

It would return a 413 for `RequestDataTooBig`, but making an `ASGIRequest` reads no body and so never raises it; any other exception it does not catch (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.create_request`).

A disconnect while the body arrives ends the request earliest: `ASGIHandler.read_body` raises `RequestAborted`, and `handle` returns before either signal (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.read_body`).
If a task the thread started on the loop with `async_to_sync` is still running, that crossing cancels it and waits for the thread (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:SyncToAsync.__call__`).

Its cancellation becomes an `asyncio.CancelledError` raised in that layer's call (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:AsyncToSync.main_wrap`): at once for an async view, which is cancelled where it awaits; for a synchronous view, which the thread runs inside that call, when the view returns.

That error is no `Exception`: `MiddlewareMixin.__call__` never reaches its `process_response`, and each layer's wrapper, catching only `Exception`, lets it through (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`).

Middleware in async mode let it through alike (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__acall__`).
